newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares extend gains, 1,200 pts next aim.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares extend gains, 1,200 pts next aim.

text.p: Austrian shares advanced on Tuesday, adding on to yesterday's solid gains, and traders expect the market to continue trading with a positive bias.
"I see the ATX at 1,250 points over the medium term," said one trader, but that the market would be capped by the expiry of April futures and options contracts next week.

"There's also still a deep-rooted fear in Europe of a retreat on Wall Street -- that's weighing down a bit on sentiment," said another trader, who nevertheless thinks the blue-chip index has room to slowly clamber up to 1,200 points.
The ATX index gained 7.84 points, or 0.67 percent, to end at 1,186.13 points with 16 shares rising, four falling and one unchanged by the close.
Microchip producer Austria Mikro Systeme stole the show, surging 7.4 percent, or 74 schillings, to 1,074. The company will present its 1996 earnings at 0830 GMT tomorrow.
Traders attributed the jump in AMS to a mixture of reacting to the U.S. semiconductor index and expectations for tomorrow's results.
"With AMS, it really all comes down to whether they've managed to turn around their two subsidiaries -- that's what people speculated on today," said one.
Also strong were VA Tech, who received an order from China worth 800 million schillings, and Boehler, who announced a higher dividend of 26 schillings for 1996 versus 25 in 1995.

Oil and chemicals group OMV was the worst performing blue chip, shedding 1.35 percent to 1,320 schillings after reporting final earnings for 1996. Austria's largest industrial group netted a 14 percent rise in profits.
The all-share Vienna bourse index gained 0.5 percent to 449.61 points.
In the futures market, the April ATX contract climbed 5.8 points to 1,184.8 on turnover of 575 contracts. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12256
